Treatment summary
Patient presented following a rear-end motor vehicle collision with reported head
impact and subsequent symptoms consistent with concussion. The mechanism and force of
the collision are well matched to the injury described. Over the course of 25 visits,
the patient received a structuerd program of symptom monitoring, cognitive rest
guidance, vestibular and oculomotor exercises, and gradual return-to-activity
planning. Treatment followed a typical clinical progression, with visit frequency and
intensity tapering as symptoms improved. Examination findings were mixed: several
measures, including balance and eye-tracking assessments, supported the diagnosis,
while other neurological screening tests returned normal results. No prior injury to
the head or neck region is known to this provider. Billing records show two similar
service charges on the same date of service, which are currently under routine review.
Patient is discharged to self-directed home exericse with instructions to return if
symptoms recur or worsen.
